newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem aide blames Cavallo for IBM bribe scandal.
newsitem.headline: Menem aide blames Cavallo for IBM bribe scandal.

text.p: Argentina's presidential Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan, accused by ex-Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo of turning a blind eye to a bribery scandal involving IBM Argentina, said Cavallo was responsible.

Kohan said in a newspaper interiew published Thursday that the blame for bribes allegedly paid by IBM's local branch for a contract at state bank Banco Nacion lay with Cavallo and ex-Banco Nacion chief Aldo Dadone, who has been indicted.
"I prefer to wait for the courts, but it seems to me that the people responsible at that time were Cavallo...and Dadone, who was his most trusted man," Kohan told Clarin newspaper.

Cavallo, sacked in July, told a federal judge this week Kohan knew bribes were paid in the $250 million contract to update computers at Argentina's biggest bank. Eleven former IBM and Nacion employees have had their indictments confirmed.
Cavallo also spoke of a meeting between Menem, Kohan and himself to discuss the scandal -- a meeting that both Menem and Kohan flatly deny ever took place.
One of Kohan's aides, Juan Carlos Cattaneo, is among those indicted for his links to a computer company that received part of the $37 million in subcontracts at the heart of the bribe scandal.
But Kohan, President Carlos Menem's top aide, said he was not even in government at the time the bribery allegedly took place in 1993. He took up his current post in 1995.
"No, I didn't know anything," he said.

Kohan said he may join Interior Minister Carlos Corach in suing Cavallo. Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan were accused by Cavallo in his latest anti-corruption crusade of covering up graft and manipulating judges. Both have denied any wrongdoing.
"If there is the possibility of suing, I will. If there is something that offends me, some lie or calumny, I will take legal action," Menem's chief of staff said.
